title: Jury Says No to Elon Musk's Lawsuit Against OpenAI
summary: Imagine giving $38 million to a friend to start a charity, and then they turn it into a business. That's what Elon Musk says happened with OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT. But a jury in California just said his lawsuit came too late. The case is over. Musk donated $38 million to help start OpenAI in 2015. He said the company promised to be a non-profit, working on AI for the good of everyone. But later, OpenAI became a for-profit company. Musk said CEO Sam Altman tricked him. In court, Musk told the jury, "It's not OK to steal a charity." But Altman said Musk knew about the plan to become a business. In fact, Altman said Musk wanted to be in charge forever. "He said maybe control should pass to his children," Altman testified. The jury listened to three weeks of arguments and looked at emails. They only needed two hours to decide. They said Musk waited too long to sue. A rule called a statute of limitations (a time limit for filing a lawsuit) had run out. OpenAI's lawyer said the jury saw that Musk was lying. A spokesman called it a "tremendous victory." So for now, OpenAI stays as it is, working on AI that it says will help all people.
why_it_matters: This case shows that even rich and famous people must follow the same rules as everyone else, including time limits for going to court, which is a lesson about fairness in our justice system.

background_read: OpenAI (the company behind the popular chatbot ChatGPT) was started in 2015. Elon Musk (the billionaire behind Tesla and SpaceX) helped create it, believing it should be a non-profit that shares AI benefits with everyone. Later, OpenAI became a for-profit business, and now Sam Altman (its CEO) is in a legal fight with Musk.
Article_Structure: WHO: Elon Musk, Sam Altman, and a jury in California.
WHAT: The jury decided Musk's lawsuit against OpenAI was too late, ending the case.
WHY: The statute of limitations, a time limit for suing, had expired.

perspectives.description: He believed OpenAI tricked him by turning a charity into a business, and felt betrayed after donating $38 million.
They argued that Musk knew about the business plans and wanted to be in charge, and that the lawsuit was filed too late.
They focused on the law and decided that Musk waited too long, regardless of who was right or wrong.
